hook_text: South Africa = gold and mines, right? The receipts say mines and farms earn less than R10 of every R100.
clip_script: Now the fact that surprises almost everyone about South Africa. Say our economy, and most people picture headgear and gold dust. Yet of every hundred rand the country produces, roughly sixty-five rand come from services, about twenty from factories and building sites, and less than ten from mines and farms combined. South Africa is a services economy that happens to own famous mines — not a mining economy with some shops attached. One trap before you go: a small rand share is not the same as a small importance. Farming contributes about three rand in a hundred, yet it fills the nation's plates and employs people in districts where no other work exists. The money scoreboard and the jobs scoreboard are different games.
visual_style: A giant R100 note sliced live on screen into three unequal strips — services towering, factories modest, a sliver for mines and farms — then a magnifying glass zooming into the sliver to reveal full dinner plates and working hands.
mood: Myth-busting, sharp, respectful of the small sliver.
pacing: Confident setup of the myth, quick-cut slicing of the note, deliberate slow zoom for the final trap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to map all three sectors and the wires and pipes they run on.
